input.query: return label fee prepaid ground label manufacturing defect

evidence.text: Who pays for a return label  For ordinary domestic change-of-mind returns, the store offers a ground label for USD 7 per parcel. If the customer uses it, USD 7 is deducted from the refund or store credit. A customer may instead arrange and pay for their own suitable carrier. A store label covers one parcel; two parcels require two labels. Membership does not waive this fee.  An approved wrong-item shipment or manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid label without the USD 7 deduction. The support team must approve that reason first. A customer selecting a defect reason in the portal is not sufficient proof that the claim has been approved. The hiking boot fit trial is a fit return, so the normal USD 7 label fee applies unless the customer supplies their own shipping.  Use suitable packaging and keep the carrier acceptance receipt. Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service.

An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label. For a paid repair, shipping is included only if the individual quotation says so. Warranty decisions apply to the specific damage inspected. A previous approved claim does not guarantee that a different problem will also be covered.

The return-label fee follows the ordinary return-label policy. A recipient may use their own carrier if they do not want to buy the store label. This article does not describe the expiration date or transferability of store credit.

searches.query: I bought a final-sale outlet tent 18 months ago. A stitching seam has now separated in normal use; this was not a disclosed outlet flaw. Does final sale prevent a warranty claim, what evidence do I need, and will an approved manufacturing-defect return cost me a label fee?

chunks.text: Outlet and final-sale products  Products marked final sale in the outlet cannot be returned merely because the customer changes their mind, chooses the wrong color, or finds a lower price later. The final-sale marking appears on the product page and the order confirmation. A general store promotion does not make a product final sale unless the product is specifically marked that way.  Final sale does not remove the manufacturing warranty. A defective outlet tent follows the tent warranty assessment process, including proof of purchase and photos. Cosmetic wear that was disclosed on the outlet listing is not a new manufacturing defect. Support must distinguish a disclosed condition from a fault that arose later.  If the delivered outlet product does not match the listing, report that problem within 14 calendar days after delivery. Keep photographs of the product and the packaging. The support team checks the listing and the received item before arranging a remedy. The 14-day mismatch report window is a separate route from the manufacturing warranty.

Tent manufacturing warranty  Tents have a 24-month warranty for manufacturing defects, beginning on the purchase date. A stitching seam that separates during normal use can qualify. The customer must provide proof of purchase and clear photos so the repair team can assess the failure. The warranty team chooses repair or replacement after assessment; support cannot promise a cash refund before that decision.  Damage from animals, sharp objects, storms beyond the tent's rating, ordinary fabric wear, or incorrect storage is outside this warranty. Accidental damage can still be sent for a paid repair assessment. A quotation must be approved before paid repair work starts. The repair-price guide lists the fixed fees that are currently published; some repairs require an individual quote.  Customers should dry a tent before packing it for inspection. Do not include fuel canisters, batteries, food, or personal belongings. An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label.

An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label. For a paid repair, shipping is included only if the individual quotation says so. Warranty decisions apply to the specific damage inspected. A previous approved claim does not guarantee that a different problem will also be covered.
